periods.analysis: Harborview held 9 community events in 2024-Q3, meeting the >=6 target and establishing a solid green baseline for this cycle. The quarter was anchored by National Night Out at Bayside Commons, two Harbor Walk safety pop-ups, three neighborhood roll-call visits, and school-readiness sessions with the North Pier and Juniper Ridge PTAs. Attendance logs and post-event cards show the strongest engagement where officers, fire prevention staff, and code outreach shared the same table rather than operating as separate stations. From a trust standpoint, this is the right start: visible, documented, and repeatable.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the quarterly operating rhythm by locking at least 8 events into the Public Safety Outreach calendar before the first month of each quarter closes. Keep using the shared sign-in and issue-tracking form so questions raised at events are routed to the correct bureau within five business days. For 2024-Q4, add one evening event on the east-side commuter corridor to balance the summer-heavy waterfront footprint.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 7 community events in 2024-Q4, down 2 from 9 in 2024-Q3 but still green against the >=6 target. The decrease is consistent with the shorter holiday operating window and the shift from outdoor plaza events to smaller indoor sessions at the Civic Center annex, Seaside Library, and Fire Station 4. Staff kept the quality controlled: each event had a designated incident-prevention topic, a Spanish-language table lead, and a documented closeout memo. The important point is that the count came down, but the procedural standard did not.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the indoor winter playbook and pre-book library, school, and faith-campus rooms at least 45 days ahead of each event. To protect the green margin, schedule one standby micro-event with the Harborview Housing Authority that can be activated if weather or staffing cancels another session. Continue capturing resident concerns by beat area so Q1 deployment briefings reflect what the community actually raised.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 9 community events in 2025-Q1, up 2 from 7 in 2024-Q4 and comfortably green against the >=6 target. The rebound came from the planned winter-to-spring outreach reset: Coffee with a Commander at Pier Market, two youth safety circles at Harborview High and East Channel Middle, and tenant-safety sessions in the Marina Vista and Alder Court complexes. The Outreach Unit also piloted event route sheets, so patrol supervisors knew which neighborhood issues had been promised follow-up before the next shift briefing. That is the kind of discipline that protects trust as the city grows.
periods.recommendations: Extend the route-sheet pilot citywide and require a named owner for every resident follow-up item before the event file is closed. Keep the Q1 level by targeting 9 events again as the default planning assumption, even though the formal target remains >=6. Add one joint event with Transportation on school-zone safety before the end of Q2 to connect enforcement, education, and engineering in the same room.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 11 community events in 2025-Q2, up 2 from 9 in 2025-Q1 and the strongest result in this run so far, remaining green against the >=6 target. The increase was planned, not accidental, with spring permit season supporting block-party safety briefings, beach-opening preparedness at South Cove, and three "Safe Routes, Safe Stops" sessions along the Route 8 and Route 14 corridors. The department used reserve officer support and CERT volunteers to avoid pulling core patrol coverage below minimum staffing. The result shows we can expand engagement while still respecting operational control.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 11-event capacity only where staffing is backfilled on the published duty roster, not through informal overtime. Convert the Route 8 and Route 14 sessions into a repeatable transit-safety module with standard handouts, translation support, and a single feedback code in the CRM. Before Q3, identify which high-attendance Q2 locations should receive return visits and which should move to annual rotation.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 9 community events in 2025-Q3, down 2 from 11 in 2025-Q2 but still green against the >=6 target. The step-down was expected after the heavy spring schedule and reflected a deliberate move from quantity to neighborhood depth during the summer tourism period. Events included National Night Out, marina patrol open-house hours, a lifeguard-and-police safety booth near Driftwood Beach, and two apartment-community meetings tied to vehicle break-in prevention. The count remains healthy, and the mix stayed aligned to seasonal risk.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the summer event floor at 9 and continue pairing each large public event with at least one smaller beat-level meeting. Use the Driftwood Beach and marina feedback to update the Q4 theft-prevention talking points before the holiday shopping period. Keep CERT and park ambassador support in the event staffing matrix so sworn personnel remain focused on safety issues that require their authority.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 7 community events in 2025-Q4, down 2 from 9 in 2025-Q3 and still green against the >=6 target. This mirrors the prior winter pattern, but the execution was cleaner because venues and staffing were reserved earlier. The quarter emphasized holiday retail safety at Harborview Town Center, package-theft prevention in the Bluffside and Canal District neighborhoods, and a senior fraud-prevention session at the Oceanview Center. We gave up some volume, but not continuity or documentation.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Q4 model by keeping retail safety, package theft, and senior fraud as the three required winter modules. Add one pre-scheduled virtual event as a weather-resilient backup, with questions logged into the same outreach tracker as in-person meetings. For 2026-Q1, carry forward the Bluffside and Canal District cohorts and report back to them on what changed from their Q4 input.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 9 community events in 2026-Q1, up 2 from 7 in 2025-Q4 and green against the >=6 target. The quarter benefited from the promised return visits to Bluffside and the Canal District, which helped close the loop on package-theft concerns and demonstrated follow-through. New events included a Harborview Community Academy cohort night, two youth diversion roundtables, and a multilingual preparedness session with the Office of Emergency Management. The pattern is now clear: when we document commitments and return with answers, participation stays durable.
periods.recommendations: Make return-reporting a standard agenda item for every recurring neighborhood event, with no more than three open commitments carried past 30 days without an update. Sustain the 9-event cadence by assigning each precinct team one community-facing event per month plus one centrally managed citywide session. Prepare Q2 expansion by reserving waterfront and school venues now, before summer demand tightens the permit calendar.

periods.analysis: Harborview held 11 community events in 2026-Q2, up 2 from 9 in 2026-Q1 and green against the >=6 target, matching the prior spring peak. The increase was supported by early venue reservations and a more mature event kit: standardized safety cards, QR-coded concern intake, and assigned follow-up captains for each beat. Programming included beach-season readiness at South Cove, bike-and-pedestrian safety near Harborview High, downtown business safety walks, and two immigrant-community listening sessions hosted with trusted nonprofit partners. This is a strong result because it shows scale with controls, not just activity.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 11-event spring capacity as the benchmark for high-demand quarters, but keep the approval gate tied to staffing, translation coverage, and follow-up capacity. Extend the QR-coded intake process to all Q3 events and review unresolved items weekly at the command staff outreach huddle. Use the two nonprofit-hosted sessions as a model for formal partner MOUs so trust-building does not depend on one-time personal relationships.

periods.analysis: Nine community events were held, down from 11 in June but above the six-event quarterly target.
periods.recommendations: Keep tracking concerns raised and closed at each event, not just the number held.
